(Check nvidia-smi)<br>- Is training speed acceptable? (Target: more than 1 step/sec)<br>- Are loss curves going down? (Check Wandb)<br>- Does reward function work independently? (Test with known inputs)<br>- Are hyperparameters reasonable? (LR: 5e-5 to 1e-4, temp: 1.0-1.5)<br>- Is dataset quality good? (No duplicates, balanced)<br>- Are generation settings correct? (max_new_tokens, temperature, top_p)</b>" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#e65100;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=15;strokeWidth=2" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="100" y="1100" width="920" height="180" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="explanation" value="<b>NON-TECHNICAL: Like debugging a car - check one system at a time (engine, brakes, fuel) until you find the problem!<br><br>TECHNICAL: Systematic debugging approach. div.b: QUICK DIAGNOSTIC CHECKLIST

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 903px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1150px; margin-left: 38px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b:
- Are rewards in expected range? (Check mean, std, min, max)
- Do outputs look reasonable? (Read a few examples)
- Is the model generating diverse responses? (Check for mode collapse)
- Is GPU memory under 90%? (Check nvidia-smi)
- Is training speed acceptable? (Target: more than 1 step/sec)
- Are loss curves going down? (Check Wandb)
- Does reward function work independently? (Test with known inputs)
- Are hyperparameters reasonable? (LR: 5e-5 to 1e-4, temp: 1.0-1.5)
- Is dataset quality good? (No duplicates, balanced)
- Are generation settings correct? (max_new_tokens, temperature, top_p)

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 903px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1315px; margin-left: 38px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b:
NON-TECHNICAL: Like debugging a car - check one system at a time (engine, brakes, fuel) until you find the problem!
TECHNICAL: Systematic debugging approach. Start with reward distribution analysis, then inspect outputs, check memory/speed, monitor training metrics. Use independent tests to isolate issues.
